course_subtitle: Welcome to the most enjoyable journey to learn the Python language! Here you will not only read, but you will live the adventure and write the magic codes yourself and see the results immediately. Unlock stations, collect badges, create your own games and drawings and become a super programmer!

stations.title: Station 1: Introduction to Python, the print function, and variables 🧱
stations.desc: Discover the fascinating history of Python, and learn the print function and variable naming rules like a pro!
stations.story:
Welcome, future hero, to the magical island of Python! 🐍 Python is a powerful and very easy to understand programming language, used in amazing fields like artificial intelligence, game development, and system protection! Today we will learn the print() function to display texts on the screen, and how to store data inside magic boxes that we call Variables!

💡 Rules for naming code boxes (Variables):
1. The name must begin with a letter only (eg name1, not 1name).
2. We do not use reserved words (such as int, if, for, print).
3. Use expressive and understandable names (such as length, not x).
4. Camel Case (such as firstName) or Pascal Case (such as FirstName).
5. Python is very case sensitive (name is completely different from Name)!
6. We connect the variable to the strings using the plus sign (+).
stations.simple: The print() function is Python's speaker! Any text you enclose in brackets and quotation marks " " will be called out loud by Python on the screen! A variable is a box in which you write a name and place a value inside it to use later.
stations.hint: Type the following magic line in the editor: print("Welcome to Megaminds Academy! 🚀") and press Run!

stations.title: Station 2: Data types, input function, and lists 🧪
stations.desc: Learn programming data types, receive user input, and master magic menus!
stations.story:
Python classifies data to understand it well! There are String (str), Integer (int), Float, and Boolean (True/False). We also learn the function of receiving inputs input() to receive the writing of heroes, and the magic lists List to store several items in one arranged box!

💡 Using parentheses in programming:
- Circular brackets (): to pass additional data or call functions.
- Square brackets []: to define and declare lists.
- Parentheses Zigzag {}: To enter dictionary values.

🎒 Magic lists (Lists) and their operations:
- Adding at the end: append()
- Adding another list: extend()
- Inserting at a specific place: insert()
- Arranging in ascending order: sort()
- Sort descending: sort(reverse=True)
- Delete: remove() or clear()
stations.simple: The data type is like the shape of a game: cube, sphere, or doll! Python needs to know the type of game to know how to play it. The List is like your color palette; You put many elements in it in order, and their indexes always start from zero (0)!

stations.title: Station 3: Arithmetic and logical operations and function design ➕
stations.desc: Learn to use arithmetic and logical operators and learn about texts such as lists and programming functions!
stations.story:
Operators are the magic symbols for operations: arithmetic (+, -, *, /), comparison (==, !=, >, <) and logical (and, or, not). We will also learn that texts are merely lists of letters arranged with indexes starting from 0, and we will learn the first concept of software functions as machines that perform specific tasks!

💡 Numerical types and conversions:
- Numbers in Python are either integer (int), decimal (float), or complex (complex).
- We can convert from one type to another easily (example: float(5) gives us 5.0).
stations.simple: Arithmetic symbols like addition and multiplication are Python's magic tools! Python can easily convert float to int and vice versa. Text, like the word "Python", is a queue of letters; The first standing letter at index 0!

stations.title: Station 4: Static class and programming dictionaries 🔒📖
stations.desc: Discover the fundamental differences between tuples and dictionaries stored with keys!
stations.story:
A tuple is a magic box for storing data, but it is never modified or changed. It is written in brackets (). As for the dictionary, it is a very intelligent store that depends on the key and the value (Key:Value), and is written with curly braces {}!

⚖️ The biggest comparison between programming structures:
- List: ordered, editable, allows repetition []
- Tuple: ordered, unmodifiable, allows repetition ()
- Dictionary: organized, editable, never allows duplicate keys {}
stations.simple: A fixed row (tuple) such as a write-protected memory card; You only read from it and you cannot edit it! The dictionary is like a phone book in which you write the name (Key) and next to the phone number (Value) so you can find it in one second without the hassle of searching in the list queues!

stations.title: Station 7: Building and designing software functions (Functions) ⚙️
stations.desc: Learn to create your own code machines using def, calling them and passing code parameters!
stations.story:
A function is an organized block of programming that only works when called! We create it using the keyword def and pass data to it called arguments and return the results with return.

💡 Arbitrary arguments and default values:
- Random arguments *args: We put an asterisk * before the name if we do not know the number of arguments passed.
- Default value: We specify a default value for the parameter if the function is called without An intermediary (such as name="hero").
stations.simple: The function is like a software juice machine! You make it once, and whenever you want fruit juice, you call it and give it the fruit (Parameters), and it gives you the delicious juice (Return) without writing the steps for cutting and squeezing again!

🔮 The magic word self:
- self is an obligatory and essential argument in any function we write inside the class. To indicate the current object that we are working on now and changing and saving its properties.
